title: Tale of the Second Attendant Kafur
summary: The second attendant, Kafur, laughed and recounted his own strange history to his companions:
keywords: tale of the second eunuch kafur
full_text:
The second attendant, Kafur, laughed and recounted his own strange history to his companions:

"I was purchased as a boy by a wealthy merchant in Aleppo. At the slave market, my former master told the buyer: 'This lad is strong, honest, and diligent, but he has one incurable flaw: once every year, he tells one single lie!' The merchant laughed, thinking: 'What harm can a single lie do in twelve months?' and paid the price.

For eleven months I served him with flawless loyalty, managing his storehouses, tending his horses, and guarding his ledger. My master praised my fidelity before all his friends. But when the twelfth month arrived, my annual impulse overcame my reason.

My master had ridden out to his country vineyard to host a banquet for his fellow merchants, leaving me to guard his city mansion. In the afternoon, I tore my tunic, smeared dust upon my head, and ran through the streets to the master's house, wailing: 'Alas! The master’s country pavilion has collapsed into the river! He and all his guests are drowned beneath the ruins!'

The mistress shrieked, broke her porcelain mirrors, tore her silken draperies, and collapsed in convulsions. The servants wept, and the neighbors gathered in lamentation. I then ran all the way to the vineyard, where my master was drinking sherbet with his companions, and shouted: 'Woe! The city mansion has caught fire, and your wife and children have perished in the flames!'

The merchant fell from his divan, tore his beard, and galloped madly toward the city. When he reached his gate, he met his wife running toward him in mourning clothes. When they discovered that both were alive and that neither house nor pavilion had suffered harm, they turned upon me in fury. 'Why did you invent such monstrous falsehoods?' roared the merchant.

I bowed meekly and replied: 'Did you not purchase me with the condition of one lie per year? Rejoice, master, for this was only a half-lie, and the year is now fulfilled!' My master, recognizing the peril of his bargain, expelled me from his house forever, proving that even a single lie can shatter a family’s peace."
moral: A single half-truth spoken out of malice can overthrow an entire household and cause irreparable ruin.

Believing rumors and flattery without proof
